patterns: how do you say why in tagalog
entries.answer: Bakit means why, and it is the word for asking for a reason. It is also used on its own as a follow-up meaning and meaning so, as in a story or a joke. Ngunit bakit is the same word in a formal sentence. It is the counterpart of ngano in the interrogative set alongside saan, kailan and sino.

patterns: how do you ask where in tagalog
entries.answer: Saan means where, and it asks about a place. Like bakit it also works as a standalone follow-up meaning and where or go on, which is very common in conversation. It is one of the four main question words in Filipino alongside bakit, kailan and sino.

patterns: how do you say when in tagalog
entries.answer: Kailan means when, and it asks about a time or a date. It is one of the four core question words in Filipino, with bakit, saan and sino. In casual speech it is often shortened by dropping the first syllable, and the full form is the one to use in writing.

patterns: how do you say who in tagalog
entries.answer: Sino means who, and it asks about a person. It is the last of the four core question words in Filipino, with bakit, saan and kailan. The word is also used in respectful address, where sinong nagsasalita means who is speaking, which carries a formality the plain form does not.

entries.answer: Ano means what, and it asks about a thing or an idea. Anong is its variant form used before a noun, as in anong libro for what book. It is the counterpart of sino, which asks about a person rather than a thing.
